citations.narrative:
Three dogs did not have identification tags assigned to them. Official identification is required and can be important to
keep track of each dog's health information. Ensure that each adult dog is assigned an identification tag that is affixed to
the animal's neck by means of a collar made of material generally considered acceptable to pet owners as a means of
identifying their pet dogs or cat.

Four puppies (two maltese puppies and two yorkie puppies; all born on 7/19/26) were in an enclosure that measured 36''
X 34" for a total of 1,224 square inches of space. The puppies measured 12'', 12.5'', 13'', and 15.5'' respectively. The four
puppies together required 1,489.5 square inches of space. Their enclosure was short by 265.5 square inches of space.
Cage space requirements ensure that the dogs have enough room to move about freely within their enclosures. It
minimizes the dogs from stepping or sitting in their feces or urine and also minimizes the spread of disease. The licensee
must ensure that all enclosures containing dogs and puppies have enough floor space to meet the minimum floor space
requirements for the number of and the size of the dogs in that enclosure.

At least 17 adult dogs are not up to date on their distemper/parvo vaccinations and 19 dogs are not up to date for their
rabies vaccinations. Not having all adult dogs up to date on their distemper/parvo and rabies vaccinations doesn't ensure
those dogs are adequately protected against those diseases that the vaccine is supposed to protect against. All adult
dogs must be vaccinated against distemper/parvo and rabies in accordance with a schedule that is approved by the
attending veterinarian.

Four dogs were heartworm tested on 9/29/26. They have documentation that four dogs were heartworm tested, but they
don't have the identification of which dogs were tested documented anywhere. Not having proper identification
documented for which dogs were tested doesn't allow for APHIS officials to be able to easily ensure the program of
veterinary care is being followed for heartworm testing. All dogs tested for heartworm must be properly identified in the
documentation for the testing.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “A” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by 11/30/26 or the applicant will forfeit the license fee and
must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
You may appeal this finding in writing by 10/8/26.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
